questions: Do these hand movements occur when you are trying to relax, or only when you're moving or focused on something else?
Did these movements start on one side first, or both hands at the same time?
Have you ever had a head injury, stroke, or been diagnosed with a movement disorder before?
Do these movements get worse when you're feeling anxious or stressed?
Do you take any medications regularly, including over-the-counter drugs?
Is there anyone else in your family who has had similar involuntary movements?
Have you noticed any stiffness, slowness, or difficulty with balance?
Did anyone ever tell you these movements are "all in your head" or suggest they might be psychological?
How old are you?
When did you first notice these movements, and have they been getting worse over time?
Have you noticed any changes in your speech, swallowing, or writing?
Have you had your eyes examined recently, and were there any abnormalities noted (e.g., rings around the cornea)?
Can you tell me how old you are in years?
Are the movements worse in one hand than the other?
When your hands are completely relaxed in your lap, do the movements continue or stop?
Do you ever notice the movements disappearing entirely for periods, such as during sleep?
Have you ever been treated for tuberculosis (TB), and did you complete the full course of treatment?
Have you had symptoms like fever, night sweats, weight loss, or a persistent cough?
Has anyone in your household been diagnosed with tuberculosis?
Have you ever been tested for HIV?
orders: Focused neurological examination of the upper limbs assessing for:
Assessment of the movements during specific tasks: finger tapping, reaching, and while the limbs are completely at rest
Head and brain MRI with contrast, specifically looking for structural lesions in the posterior fossa, cerebellum, brainstem, thalamus, and basal ganglia
Complete metabolic panel including liver function tests
